clue.text: The order for silence

parts.note: a monastic order of Cistercian monks famed for keeping a strict rule of silence

explanation.surface: Reads like a command barked to quieten a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a command to be quiet, but it is a religious order whose monks traditionally keep silence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cistercians of the Strict Observance are a religious order known for their vow of near-total silence.

clue.text: Belief that is found among them

indicators.note: found among signals the word is placed inside the letters of them

explanation.surface: A creed that is held by a certain group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found among' puts IS inside THEM, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is the conviction that a god exists, a religious creed.

clue.text: Worker goes to border county

parts.note: an ant is the standard crossword worker, from the worker ants
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: An employee heads to a frontier region.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTRIM is a county of Northern Ireland, and 'border county' hints at the Irish border.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Might outline the reflections of some holiday-makers?

definitions.text: Might outline the reflections of some holiday-makers?

parts.words: Might outline the reflections of some holiday-makers?
parts.note: a tall mirror set between windows, imagined as reflecting tourists strolling on a seaside jetty

explanation.surface: Wonders what shapes a seaside holidaymaker's thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflections' suggests thoughts, but it means mirror images; the mirror's name begins with the seaside structure where holidaymakers walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall mirror hung on the wall between two windows shows the images of those passing in front of it.

clue.text: Should get Mrs. Rae to change the order in force

indicators.note: changing these letters moves them into a different order

explanation.surface: A man tells Mrs Rae to change what the rules say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges MRS RAE to ERARMS; SHOULD stands as written. The 'force' is an armed force, where this is a drill command.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a drill command telling soldiers to bring their rifles up onto the shoulder.

clue.text: Periods of enchantment?

parts.note: the word for short stretches of time is also the word for magic charms

explanation.surface: Times when everything feels magical.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses ride on one word: a 'spell' is a stretch of time and also an enchantment.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of weather or work is a spell, and a magic charm is a spell too.

clue.text: Part of Horner's property goes to the church

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme, Little Jack Horner sat in a corner eating a Christmas pie
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Some of Mr Horner's estate is bequeathed to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: Horner is Little Jack Horner of the nursery rhyme, who pulled a plum from his pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or bit of something larger.

clue.text: A peevish entrant in the foreign game

indicators.note: an entrant goes into something, so these letters go inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
cross means irritable or peevish

explanation.surface: A grumpy newcomer to some sport played abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrant in' puts A CROSS inside LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with long netted sticks.

clue.text: Bob takes fish and fruit

parts.note: the shad is a fish of the herring family
to dock a tail is to cut it short, to bob it

explanation.surface: A man called Bob helps himself to fish and fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name but is the verb for cutting short.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaddock is a large citrus fruit, the pomelo.

clue.text: Rent collector takes fish back from warehouse

annotationWithheld.why: 'Rent collector takes fish back from warehouse' (scan agrees): EPOT is TOPE (a fish) reversed and 'warehouse' defines, but nothing in 'Rent collector' gives ENTR honestly; RENT would have to be its own anagram indicator, a word doing two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Rent collector takes fish back from warehouse

clue.text: Thanks to France, gets a kingdom

parts.note: merci is the French word for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone owes their gains to French help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thanks to France' reads as 'because of France', but it is the French for thanks. MERCIA was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was one of the major Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of early medieval England.

clue.text: Hippo, Rhino, Jumbo

parts.note: three big thick-skinned beasts, including Jumbo the famous elephant, named as members of an old zoological grouping

explanation.surface: A list of familiar zoo heavyweights.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo was a famous London Zoo elephant; the old order for thick-skinned mammals took in all three.
explanation.definitionFit: This former zoological order grouped thick-skinned hoofed mammals such as elephants, rhinoceroses and hippopotamuses.

clue.text: The drink in David's hand ?

definitions.meaning: a cocktail of spirit, usually gin, with sugar and water, as in the Singapore variety
David killed Goliath with a stone from the weapon he carried

explanation.surface: Asks what beverage King David is holding.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin cocktail is called a sling, and David's weapon against Goliath was a sling for hurling stones.

clue.text: All he does is to repair property

indicators.note: repairing something puts it back together, so these letters are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A handyman's whole job is fixing up buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to repair' rearranges the nine letters of ALL HE DOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Land or buildings held on a lease for a set term are a kind of property tenure.

clue.text: Brave a hostile reception, as players often do

definitions.meaning: to accept criticism or punishment for something done
musicians in an orchestra look at the score set before them

explanation.surface: Performers who must stand up to a booing audience.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means confronting the consequences, and literally musicians turn towards their sheet music.

clue.text: Island race that settled on an island

definitions.meaning: the island at the heart of New York City

definitions.text: race that settled on an island
definitions.meaning: a Native American people of the Lenape group who lived on that island before the Dutch came

explanation.surface: A tribe that made its home on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The borough of New York is an island, and it takes its name from the people who lived there.

clue.text: Doctor of Divinity, short of cash?

definitions.text: Doctor of Divinity, short of cash?

parts.words: Doctor of Divinity, short of cash?
parts.note: the abbreviation of the degree, two letter Ds, reads as two old pennies

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a doctorate who is hard up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of cash' looks like 'poor', but means the shortened form in money: DD, and d was the symbol for an old penny, so DD is two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: In pre-decimal British money d stood for a penny, so DD reads as a coin worth two pennies.

clue.text: Chief performer ? Rats

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: turn the word for a celebrity round and you get this word

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about the leading act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats' looks like an oath, but it is what you get when the first word of the answer is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The headline act of a show is its main attraction, the top performer on the bill.

clue.text: Resisting having some position in society

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with money
standing is one's status or rank in the community

explanation.surface: Someone holding out while enjoying social status.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand is to hold out against, so the participle means holding out or opposing.

clue.text: Wear for the dance

definitions.meaning: a short open jacket worn by women or in Spanish costume
a Spanish dance in triple time, also known from Ravel's piece

explanation.surface: Asks what to put on for a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a short jacket and a lively Spanish dance.

clue.text: Inventor turns up his nose about a girl

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the girl's name
in a down clue turning up means the word nose is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A scientist sniffs disdainfully at a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses NOSE to ESON; 'about' wraps it round DI. The idiom 'turn up one's nose' is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison patented the phonograph and an electric light bulb, among many devices.

clue.text: Send vehicle back for occasional worker

indicators.note: back tells us the whole run of letters built from these two words is read in reverse

parts.note: to remit is to send, as money by post
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: An instruction to return a car to a temp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REMIT TRAP into PART TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who works only some of the hours of a full week is employed on a casual or occasional basis.

clue.text: People securing certain ranks ?

definitions.meaning: those who fasten things with knots or bonds
rows or levels arranged one above another

explanation.surface: Folk who fasten particular rows.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who tie things are tiers, and rows stacked one above another are tiers.

clue.text: One way to abhor a vacuum ?

parts.note: a void is an empty space, a vacuum

explanation.surface: Echoes the saying that nature abhors a vacuum.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls 'nature abhors a vacuum'; split differently, A VOID gives a verb for shunning something you hate.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping away from something is one way of showing that you loathe or shun it.

clue.text: Una rectified the main ill-feeling

indicators.note: rectified means set right, so these letters are rearranged into proper order

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea

explanation.surface: A woman named Una puts right the general bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rectified' turns UNA into NAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgust or queasiness is a feeling of sickness, so it is literally an ill feeling.

clue.text: See her in trousers-they're in leopard-skins

indicators.note: in places the word her inside the word for trousers

parts.note: pants is the American (and informal) word for trousers

explanation.surface: Look at her in trousers, while others wear leopard print.
explanation.walkthrough: A black panther is a leopard, so these big cats wear leopard skin of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Panther is another name for the leopard, so these cats live inside leopard skins.

clue.text: He sounds serious

indicators.note: sounds means the word for serious is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: earnest means sincere and serious

explanation.surface: A man whose voice comes across as solemn.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest is a man's name, which is why 'He' can define it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a male first name, so a man called that could be referred to simply as a he.

clue.text: Beastly food for a son if in trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Food for a son who has got into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges A SON IF. 'Beastly' here means for beasts, not nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sainfoin is a leguminous plant grown as fodder for livestock.
